chunks: With this chain of transmission, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from a man, from Yaḥyā ibn ʿUbādah, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
“A fresh palm-strip is taken, of the length of a cubit, and it is placed”—and he gestured with his hand from near his collarbone to his hand—“wrapping it with his shrouds.”
He said: And the man said, “I later met Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام and asked him about it, and he said: ‘Yes, I had indeed narrated it to Yaḥyā ibn ʿUbādah.’”

key_terms.تَرْقُوَتِهِ: his collarbone, used to indicate the placement area by gesture
key_terms.ثِيَابِهِ: his garments or shrouds, with which it is wrapped
key_terms.جَرِيدَةٌ: a palm-strip or branch used here in funeral preparation
key_terms.حَدَّثْتُ: I narrated, indicating direct transmission of the report
key_terms.ذِرَاعٍ: a cubit, indicating the prescribed length
key_terms.رَطْبَةٌ: fresh or moist, describing the palm-strip

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about placing a fresh palm-strip with the deceased in the shroud?
ai.summary: This hadith describes a funerary practice involving a fresh palm-strip of about a cubit in length, placed with the deceased and wrapped together with the shrouds. It also includes a confirmation from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام that he had previously narrated this instruction to Yaḥyā ibn ʿUbādah, reinforcing the transmission of the ruling.
